text:
alex: seeing sudden p99 jump for ap-south-1 customers since ~12:30 UTC. latency from ~120ms -> 900-1600ms.
sarah: any errors in traces or 5xxs?
alex: some 502s reported but mostly timeouts. I grabbed a trace — shows route: client -> ap-south edge -> unexpectedly egress to us-east -> back to eu-west -> our model endpoint in us-west. weird.
mike: can you paste the trace ids?
alex: trace ids: trc-APX-221, trc-APX-222
alex: snippets:
```
path: client/ap-south-edge -> peering-us-east -> transit-eu-west -> us-west-model
latencies: [ap-south->us-east 450ms, us-east->eu-west 300ms, eu-west->us-west 380ms]
status: 200 eventually, but p99=1.2s
``` 
ingest-bot: alert: route-anomaly detected for ap-south edge at 2026-03-17T12:31:05Z (score 0.87)
sarah: running a quick traceroute from ap-south edge to model host
mike: also check egress peering table and BGP community tags, last change 2026-03-17T12:15 by deploy-bot
alex: traceroute output:
```
1  10.0.1.1
2  100.64.0.5 (ap-south-edge-router)
3  203.0.113.12 (peering-us-east)
4  198.51.100.7 (transit-eu-west)
5  198.51.100.45 (us-west-model)
``` 
sarah: looks like next-hop is the us-east peering, which is wrong for ap-south origin. did autoscaling or sticky routing flip region affinity?
mike: I rolled a peering policy change at 12:10 to migrate some capacity for maintenance but a rollback didn't fully complete. suspect route leak.
jen: any quick mitigation we can give the customer?
alex: temporary mitigation: set header `X-Preferred-Region: ap-south-1` from client or add `region_hint=ap-south-1` in API call. That forces smart-router to prefer local egress.
sarah: pushing a hotfix to revert the peering policy rollback step now.
mike: confirmed a stale BGP withdraw didn't publish, pushing proper withdraw now.
alex: customer-facing note: "We're investigating a routing issue causing higher latency for APAC customers; temporary mitigation applied. ETA ~15-30m." :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
ingest-bot: incident created: INC-20260317-APAC-HOP (severity: S3)
sarah: after fix, can you re-run traces and collect p50/p95/p99 for 30m window?
alex: will do. initial post-fix sample looks much better: p99 down to ~180ms for ap-south. will update thread with final numbers.
mike: follow-up: will open a postmortem, need to include peering change runbook gap and verify canary coverage on routing changes.
jen: thanks team, cc'ing customer success to update customers.
alex: updated numbers: 30m post-fix p50=35ms p95=80ms p99=190ms. closing for now unless we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
